pathway.title: Mativ Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate rather than strong. Net sales in 2025 were 1.92% below 2023, gross margin has risen to 19.58% in the first nine months of 2026 from 18.09%, and no customer reaches 10% of sales, but volume and mix fell 4.4% in the first nine months of 2026, so price rather than demand carried the gain. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C12

Leverage is falling but still high and coverage is thin. Net debt of USD 879.1 million is 4.43x reported trailing EBITDA of USD 198.6 million, against 7.13x at the end of 2024, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 80.1 million only 2.48x. The company reports net leverage of 3.8x against a 5.00x covenant maximum on definitions the filings do not print, and trailing adjusted EBITDA is not established, so the two measures cannot be reconciled. Pro forma net debt and net leverage for the November 4, 2026 facility sale and the December 18, 2026 dividend are not established, because the Financial foundation states none. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

Cash generation is the main support but it cannot repay the debt on its own. Free cash flow was USD 98.5 million over the last twelve months, capital spending ran at only 0.53x depreciation in 2025, and the dividend took 18.78% of nine-month free cash flow. At the twelve-month rate, repaying net debt would take 8.93 years. Third-quarter free cash flow of USD 37.5 million was 43.78% below the prior-year quarter. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex991earningsrelease2026q3.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C17; calculation C21; calculation C22

Liquidity is adequate but smaller than a year ago. Cash of USD 97.3 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 276.2 million give USD 373.5 million against scheduled repayments of only USD 14.9 million to 2028, yet the committed revolver was cut from USD 600.0 million to USD 305.0 million in April 2026 and liquidity was USD 515.4 million at the end of 2025. Letters of credit drawn on the revolver are not itemised, and pro forma cash for the facility sale of November 4, 2026, whose proceeds are not stated, is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation C7; calculation C23

Refinancing is the decisive risk. The USD 400.0 million senior unsecured notes due 2029 rank behind facilities secured on substantially all personal property, and while the notes stay outstanding the revolver and Term Loan A mature 182 days, and Term Loan B 91 days, before them. Up to USD 996.2 million of principal would then fall due during 2029, the facilities in April and July and the notes on October 1, unless the notes are refinanced or extended first. The notes' quoted fair value was 99.7% of principal at the end of September 2026, a sign that the market was not pricing distress then; no later quote is supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C24

Financial policy is mixed to supportive, and the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium. There is no sponsor, the dividend is modest and was cut, no shares were repurchased in 2025 or the third quarter of 2026, and the lenders agreed to refinance USD 894.9 million of facilities in April 2026; against that, management states a pivot to growth and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so what the company may do with cash is not assessed. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex991earningsrelease2026q3.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C26

Adjusted earnings run ahead of reported earnings, which flatters any adjusted leverage. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 184.8 million exceeds reported EBITDA of USD 157.1 million by USD 27.7 million, and the add-backs include financing fees on the receivables programme, whose USD 837.3 million of sales in nine months 2026, 55.42% of net sales, sit outside reported debt. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex991earningsrelease2026q3.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex991earningsrelease2026q3.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15; calculation C18

The primary downside is further volume loss in the lower-margin segment, which would hurt refinancing before it hurt liquidity. Repeating the third-quarter fall in segment gross profit of USD 10.7 million for four quarters would cut trailing reported EBITDA to USD 155.8 million, lift net leverage to 5.64x and cut interest cover to 1.95x, while free cash flow would stay positive at USD 55.7 million before dividends. This is an analyst scaling of one observed quarter, not a forecast. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C10

runs.text: The first strength is diversification: no customer reached 10% of net sales in 2023 to 2025 and no product category exceeded 30% of nine-month 2026 sales, so the loss of one account or one line cannot remove a large share of cash flow, which supports revenue durability and debt service. The second is the recovery in margin and cash flow: gross margin of 19.58% against 18.09%, adjusted EBITDA up 7.94% and free cash flow of USD 90.5 million in nine months show price and cost actions working, which supports interest cover. The third is liquidity and a clear maturity runway: USD 373.5 million of cash and undrawn revolver against only USD 14.9 million of scheduled repayments to 2028 means no maturity forces a refinancing before 2029. The fourth is restrained financial policy: a dividend of USD 0.10 per share a quarter that was cut from the 2023 level, no repurchases in 2025 or the third quarter of 2026, and past disposal proceeds applied to debt, which keeps cash in the business for lenders. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex991earningsrelease2026q3.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C23

The first weakness is the 2029 refinancing: up to USD 996.2 million of principal falls due in 2029 if the notes are still outstanding when the springing dates arrive, so access to capital markets in 2027 and 2028 decides the outcome for creditors. The second is leverage and cover: net debt of 4.43x reported trailing EBITDA and cover of 2.48x leave little room for an earnings setback. The third is weak volume: volume and mix fell 4.4% in nine months 2026 and sales in the lower-margin segment fell 10.9% in the third quarter, partly on the tornado, so earnings growth depends on price. The fourth is reliance on selling receivables, USD 837.3 million in nine months 2026, whose outstanding balance is not printed, so debt-like funding sits outside reported debt. The fifth is a thin equity cushion: tangible equity is negative at USD 48.7 million after goodwill write-offs of USD 812.9 million, and the segment with the remaining goodwill had only about 6% headroom at its last test. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C18; calculation C19

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The group in its present form came from the merger completed on July 6, 2022 of Schweitzer-Mauduit International and Neenah, after which Neenah survives as a direct wholly owned subsidiary and the parent was renamed Mativ Holdings. The group was then reshaped by the sale of the Engineered Papers business to Evergreen Hill Enterprise for USD 620.0 million in cash on November 30, 2023, which carried a gain of USD 176.3 million, repaid about USD 641.2 million of debt and ended participation in tobacco-based markets. The consideration and financing of the 2022 merger are not stated in the supplied documents. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4

The newest debt is the refinancing under the Ninth Amendment dated April 3, 2026, which replaced the revolving facility, Term Loan A and Term Loan B and eliminated the delayed draw term loan. It provides committed facilities of about USD 894.9 million, made up of a USD 305.0 million revolver, a USD 89.9 million Term Loan A and a USD 500.0 million Term Loan B, and it produced a USD 8.7 million loss on extinguishment, with USD 32.7 million of debt issuance costs paid in the first nine months of 2026. The revolver and Term Loan A mature on the earlier of five years from April 3, 2026 and 182 days before the 2029 notes mature, and Term Loan B on the earlier of seven years and 91 days before. Margins on the revolver and Term Loan A range from 1.75% to 2.75% by net leverage, Term Loan B margins are fixed at 3.50% to 4.50% by benchmark, and the financial covenants apply only to the revolver and Term Loan A. Three subsidiaries became additional U.S. borrowers and one more became a guarantor. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-03-31_matv-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22

No bond was issued in 2026. The USD 400.0 million senior unsecured notes due October 1, 2029 were issued on October 7, 2024, are redeemable at the company's option on or after October 1, 2026 and remain the only bond; the use of the proceeds is not stated in the supplied documents. After the quarter, on October 23, 2026 the receivables sales agreement was amended to extend its term to October 23, 2029, with its commitment size not printed, and on November 4, 2026 a North American facility held for sale was sold, with proceeds not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership, operating model and governance fact pack for Mativ Holdings, Inc. (ticker MATV) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers what the company does, how it reached its present shape, who owns and controls it, and how it has treated lenders and shareholders. It makes no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mativ is a listed specialty materials producer with no sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder named in the supplied documents, so creditor risk rests on operating execution and shareholder-return policy rather than on sponsor extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_matv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The diversified customer base, with no customer at 10% of sales, supports cash flow, and the dividend of USD 17.0 million paid in the first nine months of 2026 was 18.78% of free cash flow of USD 90.5 million. Against that, two goodwill write-offs totalling USD 812.9 million, a July 2026 tornado that contributed to a 10.9% fall in third-quarter sales in Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, and management's stated pivot to growth keep the case open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership gives creditors no sponsor whose exit or fee incentives must be underwritten, and no sponsor to rely on for support: the company has been listed since its 1995 spin-off from Kimberly-Clark, and directors and officers together hold about 0.40% of the shares on the run's own arithmetic. The holdings of large institutions are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied, so the absence of a controlling holder is the filings' silence, not a confirmed fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified by segment, product and customer, which supports revenue durability, but the lower-margin segment carries most of the sales. Filtration & Advanced Materials was about 39% of 2025 sales and Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions about 61%; nine-month 2026 gross margin was 22.81% in the first and 17.41% in the second, and no product category exceeded 30% of nine-month sales. The United States was 56.17% of 2025 sales, so American demand carries most of the revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's history is acquisition followed by write-down and pruning, and that is the main governance fact for creditors. The 2022 merger with Neenah created the group; goodwill impairments of USD 401.0 million in 2023 and USD 411.9 million in 2025 show that purchase value did not hold, and all goodwill of the Filtration & Advanced Materials unit was written off after its discount rate was raised to 14%. The 2023 sale of the Engineered Papers business for USD 620.0 million in cash repaid about USD 641.2 million of debt, and the supplied filings disclose no acquisition since. Equity of USD 467.1 million rests on goodwill and intangible assets: tangible equity is negative at USD 48.7 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder distributions are modest and were cut, so they are not the main risk, but they continue while reported net leverage is 3.8x. The dividend fell from USD 1.00 per share in 2023 to USD 0.40 in 2024 and 2025, a cut of 60%; cash dividends were USD 22.3 million in 2025 and USD 17.0 million in the first nine months of 2026, and no shares were repurchased in 2025 or in the third quarter of 2026, with USD 22.0 million of the authorisation unused. A further USD 0.10 per share payable on December 18, 2026 is about USD 5.52 million on the run's arithmetic.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Documented behaviour towards lenders is mixed to supportive rather than adverse, but the legal room for other behaviour is untested. The credit agreement was amended in December 2024 and refinanced in April 2026 into committed facilities of USD 894.9 million, with USD 32.7 million of debt issuance costs paid and a USD 8.7 million loss on extinguishment in the first nine months of 2026, and the supplied documents disclose no waiver, exchange, priming or non-pro-rata transaction. The revolver and Term Loan A mature 182 days, and Term Loan B 91 days, before the 2029 notes if those are still outstanding, and the maximum net debt to EBITDA covenant steps down from 5.00x to 4.00x by mid-2028. The executed credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so what they permit is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion rests partly on selling trade receivables, which is the operating feature that most needs monitoring. USD 837.3 million of receivables were sold in the first nine months of 2026, equal to 55.42% of net sales, they leave reported debt, and the programme's term was extended to October 23, 2029 on October 23, 2026. The balance owed under it is not printed, and the company adds the programme's financing fees of USD 5.1 million back to adjusted EBITDA, so reported leverage excludes a debt-like funding claim that cannot be sized from the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The July 2026 Menasha tornado is the one operating shock in the period and it landed in the lower-margin segment. Sales in Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions fell 10.9% in the third quarter, which the company attributes primarily to the tornado and to healthcare, and its adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 11.6% from 13.7%; the company recorded an inventory write-off of USD 42.5 million against an insurance recovery receivable of USD 38.0 million and recoveries received of USD 5.0 million, a net loss of USD 0.8 million. Recovery of the receivable is the company's expectation, and recoveries beyond inventory are not recognised.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_matv-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_ex991earningsrelease2026q3.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C15; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management turnover raises execution risk, while reporting and audit quality are supportive. The chief executive took office in March 2025 and a new chief financial officer in January 2026, with USD 7.6 million of one-time separation costs in 2025; against that, the auditor's opinion is unqualified, internal control over financial reporting is effective, quarterly reports follow period end within 36 to 37 days, and the annual report is filed within 57 days. Board composition and related-person transactions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sponsor and governance risk level is Medium. It is driven by dividends continuing at reported net leverage of 3.8x, two credit agreement amendments in 2024 and 2026, executive turnover and a stated pivot to growth, which together leave leverage priorities open; it is held back from High by modest distributions, no buybacks, no disclosed lender-adverse behaviour and a lower dividend than in 2023. Further analysis needs the proxy statement and the executed debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is operating momentum and deleveraging. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA was USD 184.8 million, 7.94% above the prior year, free cash flow was USD 90.5 million, reported net leverage fell from 4.2x at the end of 2025 to 3.8x, and the company reports compliance with every covenant. The company also describes reducing leverage as a priority and says it expects inventory losses from the tornado to be fully recoverable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The group in its present form came from the merger completed on July 6, 2022 of Schweitzer-Mauduit International and Neenah, after which Neenah survives as a direct wholly owned subsidiary and the parent was renamed Mativ Holdings. The group was then reshaped by the sale of the Engineered Papers business to Evergreen Hill Enterprise for USD 620.0 million in cash on November 30, 2023, which carried a gain of USD 176.3 million, repaid about USD 641.2 million of debt and ended participation in tobacco-based markets. The consideration and financing of the 2022 merger are not stated in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The newest debt is the refinancing under the Ninth Amendment dated April 3, 2026, which replaced the revolving facility, Term Loan A and Term Loan B and eliminated the delayed draw term loan. It provides committed facilities of about USD 894.9 million, made up of a USD 305.0 million revolver, a USD 89.9 million Term Loan A and a USD 500.0 million Term Loan B, and it produced a USD 8.7 million loss on extinguishment, with USD 32.7 million of debt issuance costs paid in the first nine months of 2026. The revolver and Term Loan A mature on the earlier of five years from April 3, 2026 and 182 days before the 2029 notes mature, and Term Loan B on the earlier of seven years and 91 days before. Margins on the revolver and Term Loan A range from 1.75% to 2.75% by net leverage, Term Loan B margins are fixed at 3.50% to 4.50% by benchmark, and the financial covenants apply only to the revolver and Term Loan A. Three subsidiaries became additional U.S. borrowers and one more became a guarantor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No bond was issued in 2026. The USD 400.0 million senior unsecured notes due October 1, 2029 were issued on October 7, 2024, are redeemable at the company's option on or after October 1, 2026 and remain the only bond; the use of the proceeds is not stated in the supplied documents. After the quarter, on October 23, 2026 the receivables sales agreement was amended to extend its term to October 23, 2029, with its commitment size not printed, and on November 4, 2026 a North American facility held for sale was sold, with proceeds not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Mativ Holdings, Inc. (ticker MATV) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. It weighs business quality, cash generation, liquidity, leverage, refinancing capacity and financial policy of the consolidated group into one creditor view and the monitoring points that would change it. It assigns no rating and makes no security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mativ is an adequately liquid and diversified specialty-materials credit with falling leverage, so near-term debt service looks secure, but the 2029 notes pull about USD 996.2 million of principal into one refinancing, which is the decisive risk for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 879.1 million is 4.43x reported trailing EBITDA, against 3.8x on the company's covenant basis, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.48x, so the cushions are thin; liquidity of USD 373.5 million and free cash flow of USD 98.5 million over twelve months buy time. Pro forma net debt for the November 2026 facility sale and the December 2026 dividend is not established.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate rather than strong. Net sales in 2025 were 1.92% below 2023, gross margin has risen to 19.58% in the first nine months of 2026 from 18.09%, and no customer reaches 10% of sales, but volume and mix fell 4.4% in the first nine months of 2026, so price rather than demand carried the gain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is falling but still high and coverage is thin. Net debt of USD 879.1 million is 4.43x reported trailing EBITDA of USD 198.6 million, against 7.13x at the end of 2024, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 80.1 million only 2.48x. The company reports net leverage of 3.8x against a 5.00x covenant maximum on definitions the filings do not print, and trailing adjusted EBITDA is not established, so the two measures cannot be reconciled. Pro forma net debt and net leverage for the November 4, 2026 facility sale and the December 18, 2026 dividend are not established, because the Financial foundation states none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the main support but it cannot repay the debt on its own. Free cash flow was USD 98.5 million over the last twelve months, capital spending ran at only 0.53x depreciation in 2025, and the dividend took 18.78% of nine-month free cash flow. At the twelve-month rate, repaying net debt would take 8.93 years. Third-quarter free cash flow of USD 37.5 million was 43.78% below the prior-year quarter.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but smaller than a year ago. Cash of USD 97.3 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 276.2 million give USD 373.5 million against scheduled repayments of only USD 14.9 million to 2028, yet the committed revolver was cut from USD 600.0 million to USD 305.0 million in April 2026 and liquidity was USD 515.4 million at the end of 2025. Letters of credit drawn on the revolver are not itemised, and pro forma cash for the facility sale of November 4, 2026, whose proceeds are not stated, is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing is the decisive risk. The USD 400.0 million senior unsecured notes due 2029 rank behind facilities secured on substantially all personal property, and while the notes stay outstanding the revolver and Term Loan A mature 182 days, and Term Loan B 91 days, before them. Up to USD 996.2 million of principal would then fall due during 2029, the facilities in April and July and the notes on October 1, unless the notes are refinanced or extended first. The notes' quoted fair value was 99.7% of principal at the end of September 2026, a sign that the market was not pricing distress then; no later quote is supplied.

There is no sponsor, the dividend is modest and was cut, no shares were repurchased in 2025 or the third quarter of 2026, and the lenders agreed to refinance USD 894.9 million of facilities in April 2026; against that, management states a pivot to growth and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so what the company may do with cash is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside is further volume loss in the lower-margin segment, which would hurt refinancing before it hurt liquidity. Repeating the third-quarter fall in segment gross profit of USD 10.7 million for four quarters would cut trailing reported EBITDA to USD 155.8 million, lift net leverage to 5.64x and cut interest cover to 1.95x, while free cash flow would stay positive at USD 55.7 million before dividends. This is an analyst scaling of one observed quarter, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against treating refinancing as the decisive risk is market and bank support. The notes' fair value was 99.7% of principal at the end of September 2026, against 100.9% at the end of 2025, and the banks agreed in April 2026 to USD 894.9 million of facilities with stated maturities as late as 2031 and 2033 if the notes are dealt with first. Reported net leverage of 3.8x and free cash flow of USD 90.5 million in the first nine months of 2026 also show debt being reduced, if slowly.

fields.value: The view would turn more positive if the notes were refinanced or extended before the springing dates, or if trailing adjusted EBITDA showed leverage below the company's 3.8x. It would turn more negative if fourth-quarter net sales fall below the USD 463.1 million of the fourth quarter of 2025, if the USD 38.0 million insurance receivable is not collected, if liquidity falls below USD 373.5 million, or if the dividend is raised or acquisitions are funded with debt while leverage stays near current levels.

fields.value: The sections below follow the report selectors and hold every row and column the method requires; amounts are in USD millions unless a cell says otherwise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is diversification: no customer reached 10% of net sales in 2023 to 2025 and no product category exceeded 30% of nine-month 2026 sales, so the loss of one account or one line cannot remove a large share of cash flow, which supports revenue durability and debt service. The second is the recovery in margin and cash flow: gross margin of 19.58% against 18.09%, adjusted EBITDA up 7.94% and free cash flow of USD 90.5 million in nine months show price and cost actions working, which supports interest cover. The third is liquidity and a clear maturity runway: USD 373.5 million of cash and undrawn revolver against only USD 14.9 million of scheduled repayments to 2028 means no maturity forces a refinancing before 2029. The fourth is restrained financial policy: a dividend of USD 0.10 per share a quarter that was cut from the 2023 level, no repurchases in 2025 or the third quarter of 2026, and past disposal proceeds applied to debt, which keeps cash in the business for lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is the 2029 refinancing: up to USD 996.2 million of principal falls due in 2029 if the notes are still outstanding when the springing dates arrive, so access to capital markets in 2027 and 2028 decides the outcome for creditors. The second is leverage and cover: net debt of 4.43x reported trailing EBITDA and cover of 2.48x leave little room for an earnings setback. The third is weak volume: volume and mix fell 4.4% in nine months 2026 and sales in the lower-margin segment fell 10.9% in the third quarter, partly on the tornado, so earnings growth depends on price. The fourth is reliance on selling receivables, USD 837.3 million in nine months 2026, whose outstanding balance is not printed, so debt-like funding sits outside reported debt. The fifth is a thin equity cushion: tangible equity is negative at USD 48.7 million after goodwill write-offs of USD 812.9 million, and the segment with the remaining goodwill had only about 6% headroom at its last test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mativ makes engineered media for filtration, tapes and liners, specialty paper and packaging, advanced films and healthcare products, and sells in two segments: Filtration & Advanced Materials, which was about 39% of 2025 net sales and sells largely direct to system integrators, and Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, about 61% and sold through distributors, converters and retailers. Products are qualified by customers over long cycles, no customer reaches 10% of sales, and the United States is 56.17% of sales, which supports cash-flow visibility and refinancing confidence but leaves the group tied to construction, automotive and consumer cycles. The group was assembled by the 2022 merger with Neenah, shaped by the 2023 sale of the Engineered Papers business, and weakened by goodwill write-offs in 2023 and 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mativ is a listed company with no sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder named, so there is no sponsor support or extraction to weigh; the business and governance review sets the sponsor and governance risk level at Medium on a modest dividend, two credit agreement amendments, executive turnover and a stated pivot to growth. Guarantor subsidiaries that borrow under or guarantee the secured facilities also guarantee the notes, and the facilities are secured on substantially all personal property of the company and its domestic subsidiaries, so the notes are unsecured and rank behind roughly 60.17% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is stable but not growing: net sales were USD 2,026.0 million in 2023, USD 1,981.1 million in 2024 and USD 1,987.0 million in 2025, and USD 1,510.9 million in nine months 2026, down 0.9%, with volume and mix down 4.4%, price up 2.5% and currency up 1.0%. Organic growth was negative 0.4% in the first quarter, positive 1.7% in the second and negative 2.3% in the third, so volume has not yet recovered and price is the driver. Filtration & Advanced Materials grew 10.2% in the third quarter on aerospace, defense and transportation demand, which management calls its strongest sales growth, while the other segment fell 10.9%. Revenue is cyclical in construction, infrastructure and automotive end markets, partly recurring through qualified products, and exposed to substitution by lower-cost substrates in less demanding uses. Pricing power is demonstrated in 2026 but untested in a volume downturn, which makes the margin gain less certain to persist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of products sold was 80.4% of net sales in nine months 2026, so the base is mostly variable but leaves little buffer: resin is the largest single raw material cost in Filtration & Advanced Materials and wood pulp in Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, and a 10% change in resin and pulp prices would move annual pre-tax earnings by about USD 32.3 million with no price pass-through, which is 16.26% of trailing reported EBITDA. Inventories of 60 to 80 days create a lag before cost changes reach the income statement, specialty inputs come from few suppliers, and nonmanufacturing costs fell 4.7% under the realignment plan, with a further USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million of savings targeted by the end of 2026. Margins can be defended against input shocks only if price follows cost; they are weakest against volume loss in the lower-margin segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending was USD 40.0 million in 2025 against depreciation of USD 74.9 million, and USD 26.9 million in nine months 2026, so cash conversion is helped by low reinvestment that may defer equipment renewal. Free cash flow was USD 90.5 million in nine months, 48.97% of adjusted EBITDA of USD 184.8 million, after cash interest, taxes, restructuring cash and working capital; nine-month working capital was an inflow of USD 11.9 million, helped by payables rising to USD 219.6 million from USD 160.7 million, and the first quarter used cash, with free cash flow of negative USD 7.4 million. Sales of receivables of USD 837.3 million fund part of the conversion. EBITDA translates into free cash flow adequate for debt service and dividends but not for retirement of the debt before 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate: the annual report names large competitors such as 3M, Covestro, Ahlstrom and Mondi and says some are larger and some, in China, may have lower costs, but products compete on features, innovation and service. Entry is slowed by qualification cycles and over 1,100 patents and applications, substitutes threaten only the less demanding uses, buyers are dispersed with retail and distributor channels in the larger segment, and suppliers of specialty resins and mercerized pulp are few, which gives them leverage over cost. Among external factors, tariffs, currency and European energy cost matter to credit: tariffs have raised cost of goods sold, the Supreme Court ruling of February 20, 2026 on emergency-powers tariffs had a not significant net refund effect to September 30, 2026, a large share of sales is in euros and sterling, a 100 basis point rise in rates would have cost USD 1.5 million a year after hedges at the end of 2025, and at September 30, 2026 swaps covered 66.70% of floating-rate principal. Technology and social factors are not primary credit drivers on the documents supplied. In credit terms the strengths are diversification, margin recovery, liquidity and restrained distributions; the weaknesses are the 2029 wall, leverage, weak volume and thin equity; the opportunities are aerospace, defense, filtration and healthcare demand and cost savings, and the threats are input costs, tariffs, construction and automotive cycles and a second operational disruption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the fourth quarter is seasonally the weakest, with 2025 net sales by difference of USD 463.1 million, 9.85% below the third quarter, and recovery of the tornado write-off and the receivable of USD 38.0 million is expected by management but not yet collected; cost savings of USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million and the cut dividend support cash, while the smaller revolver, a Term Loan B margin of 3.50% to 4.50% against 2.75% over the reference rate before, and deferred gains of USD 4.9 million on settled swaps that are due to lower interest expense over the next twelve months shape interest cost. Management gives no numeric outlook, only confidence that full-year performance will exceed the prior year. Over three to five years the filtration, water, aerospace, healthcare and tape markets are described as growing and the paper and packaging lines as mature; the 2029 notes and the springing facility dates are the dominant event, and amortisation of intangible assets of USD 61.2 million in 2026 falling to USD 51.1 million in 2030 is non-cash. Tailwinds are price, cost savings and end-market growth in the smaller segment; headwinds are volume, tariffs, input costs and the maturity wall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is another loss of volume or distribution in Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, as the July 27, 2026 tornado showed, with no insurance recovery beyond the write-off. In the third quarter that segment's sales fell USD 34.4 million and its gross profit fell USD 10.7 million; repeating that gross profit loss for four quarters cuts trailing reported EBITDA from USD 198.6 million to USD 155.8 million, so net leverage on that basis would rise from 4.43x to 5.64x and interest cover would fall from 2.48x to 1.95x. Free cash flow would fall from USD 98.5 million to about USD 55.7 million before taxes saved and management levers, and USD 33.2 million after the dividend, so liquidity of USD 373.5 million and repayments of only USD 14.9 million to 2028 would hold. Levers include suspending the USD 22.5 million annual dividend, cutting capital spending that is already low, pulling back working capital and the cost programme. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis but the refinancing of the 2029 notes would be harder at 5.64x, and the covenant consequences are not established because the definitions are not printed. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter sales below USD 463.1 million, a fall in free cash flow and a delay to refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Mativ presents an adequate business profile supported by diversified customers, recovering margins and adequate near-term liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 4.43x on reported EBITDA, interest cover of 2.48x, weak volume and a thin equity cushion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow of USD 98.5 million covers interest, capital spending and a small dividend, though not enough to repay debt before 2029. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the notes being refinanced or extended before the springing dates, on trailing earnings showing leverage at or below the company's 3.8x, and on the receivables programme staying in place. The primary downside path is a volume and margin loss in the lower-margin segment that raises leverage ahead of the refinancing. Further analysis would require trailing adjusted EBITDA, the executed debt documents, the receivables programme balance and a peer set. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: refinancing of the 2029 maturities.
